paragraphs.sourceText: Self-image is the picture you have of yourself, the sort of person you believe you are 26 in our self-image are the categories in which you place yourself, the roles you play, and other 27 descriptors you use to identify yourself. If you tell an 28 you are a grandfather who recently lost his wife and who does 29 work on weekends, several elements of your self-image are brought to light —the roles of grandparent, widower, and 30 citizen.

But self-image is more than how you picture yourself; it also involves how others see you. Three types of feedback from others 31 how they see us: confirmation, rejection, and disconfirmation. Confirmation occurs when others treat you in a manner consistent with who you believe you are. You believe you have leadership abilities and your boss put you in charge of a new work team. On the other hand, rejection occurs when others treat you in a manner that 32 your self-definition. Pierre Salinger was appointed senator from California but 33 lost his first election. He thought he was a good public official, but the voters obviously thought otherwise —their vote was inconsistent with his 34 . The third type of feedback is disconfirmation, which occurs when others fail to respond to your notion of self by responding neutrally. A student writes what he thinks is an excellent composition, but the teacher writes no encouraging remarks. Rather than 35 how others classify you, consider how you identify yourself. The way in which you identify yourself is the best reflection of your self-image.

paragraphs.sourceText: Proper street behaviour in the United States requires a nice balance of attention and inattention. You are supposed to look at a passerby just enough to show that you are aware of his 36 If you look too little, you appear haughty(目中无人的), too much and you are inquisitive（过分好奇地）.Usually what happens is that people eye each other until they are about eight feet apart, at which point both cast down their eyes. Sociologist Erving Goffman describes this as “a kind of 37 of lights”.

Much of eye behaviour is so 38 that we react to it only on the intuitive level. The next time you have a conversation with someone who makes you feel liked, notice what he does with his eyes. Chances are he looks at you more often than is usual with 39 a little longer than the normal. You 40 this as a sign — a polite one — that he is interested in you as a person rather than just in the topic of conversation. Probably you also feel that he is both self-confident and sincere.

All this has been demonstrated in 41 experiments. Subjects sit and talk in the psychologist’s laboratory, 42 of the fact that their eye behaviour is being observed from a one way vision screen. In one fairly typical experiment, subjects were 43 to cheat while performing a task, then were interviewed and observed. It was found that those who had cheated met the interviewer’s eyes less often than was 44 , an indication that “shifty eyes” — to use the mystery writers’ stock phrase — can 45 be a tip-off(表明）to an attempt to deceive or to feelings of guilt.

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. A Nation That’s Losing Its Toolbox
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。一个正在失去工具箱的国家

paragraphs.sourceText: A) The scene inside the Home Depot on Weyman Avenue here would give the old-time American craftsman pause. In Aisle 34 is precut plastic flooring, the glue already in place. In Aisle 26 are prefabricated windows. Stacked near the checkout counters, and as colourful as a Fisher-Price toy, is a not-so-serious-looking power tool: a battery-operated saw-and-drill combination. And if you don’t want to do it yourself, head to Aisle 23 or Aisle 35, where a help desk will arrange for an installer.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 韦曼大道家得宝 (Home Depot) 内的场景会让这位美国老工匠停下来。 34 号过道是预先切割好的塑料地板，胶水已经就位。 26 号过道设有预制窗户。收银台附近堆放着一种看起来不那么严肃的电动工具，它像费雪玩具一样色彩缤纷：一种电池供电的锯钻组合。如果您不想自己动手，请前往 23 号通道或 35 号通道，服务台会在那里安排安装人员。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) It’s all very handy stuff, I guess, a convenient way to be a do-it-yourselfer without being all that good with tools. But at a time when the American factory seems to be a shrinking presence, and when good manufacturing jobs have vanished,
paragraphs.translationZh: B）我想，这都是非常方便的东西，是一种方便的方式，可以让你自己动手，而不必那么擅长使用工具。但在美国工厂的存在似乎正在萎缩、良好的制造业工作岗位消失之际，

paragraphs.sourceText: perhaps never to return, there is something deeply troubling about this dilution of American craftsmanship.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许永远不会再回来了，美国工艺的这种淡化确实令人深感不安。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) This isn’t a lament(伤感) — or not merely a lament — for bygone times. It’s a social and cultural issue, as well as an economic one. The Home Depot approach to craftsmanship — simplify it, dumb it down, hire a contractor— is one signal that mastering tools and working with one’s hands is receding in America as a hobby, as a valued skill, as a cultural influence that shaped thinking and behaviour in vast sections of the country.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 这不是对过去时代的哀叹——或者不仅仅是哀叹。这是一个社会和文化问题，也是一个经济问题。家得宝的工艺方法——简化它、简化它、雇用承包商——是一个信号，表明掌握工具和用手工作在美国作为一种爱好、一种有价值的技能、一种塑造美国大部分地区思维和行为的文化影响力正在逐渐消失。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) That should be a matter of concern in a presidential election year. Yet neither Barack Obama nor Mitt Romney promotes himself as tool-savvy(使用工具很在行的）presidential timber, in the mold of a Jimmy Carter, a skilled carpenter and cabinet maker. The Obama administration does worry publicly about manufacturing, a first cousin of craftsmanship. When the Ford Motor Company, for example, recently announced that it was bringing some production home, the White House cheered. “When you see things like Ford moving new production from Mexico to Detroit, instead of the other way around, you know things are changing,” says Gene Sperling, director of the National Economic Council.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 这应该是总统选举年值得关注的问题。然而，巴拉克·奥巴马和米特·罗姆尼都没有以吉米·卡特（Jimmy Carter）为榜样，将自己宣传为精通工具的总统木材，他是一位熟练的木匠和橱柜制造商。奥巴马政府确实公开担心制造业，而制造业是手工艺的远亲。例如，当福特汽车公司最近宣布将部分生产带回国内时，白宫欢呼雀跃。“当你看到像福特这样的公司将新生产从墨西哥转移到底特律，而不是相反时国家经济委员会主任吉恩·斯珀林 (Gene Sperling) 表示：“你知道事情正在发生变化。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Ask the administration or the Republicans or most academics why America needs more manufacturing, and they respond that manufacturing gives birth to innovation, brings down the trade deficit, strengthens the dollar, generates jobs, arms the military and brings about a recovery from recession. But rarely, if ever, do they publicly take the argument a step further, asserting that a growing manufacturing sector encourages craftsmanship and that craftsmanship is, if not a birthright, then a vital ingredient of the American self-image as a can-do, inventive, we-can-make-anything people.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）询问政府或共和党人或大多数学者为什么美国需要更多的制造业，他们的回答是制造业催生创新，降低贸易逆差，升值美元，创造就业机会，武装军队并带来经济衰退复苏。但他们很少（如果有的话）公开更进一步地提出这一论点，声称不断发展的制造业鼓励手工艺，而手工艺即使不是与生俱来的权利，也是美国人自我形象的一个重要组成部分，即美国人作为一个可以做的、有创造力的、我们可以制造任何东西的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Traditional vocational training in public high schools is gradually declining, stranding thousands of young people who seek training for a craft without going to college. Colleges, for their part, have since 1985 graduated fewer chemical, mechanical, industrial and metallurgical(冶金的）engineers, partly in response to the reduced role of manufacturing, a big employer of them. The decline started in the 1950s, when manufacturing generated a sturdy 28% of the national income, or gross domestic product, and employed one-third of the workforce. Today, factory output generates just 12% of GDP and employs barely 9% of the nation’s workers.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 公立高中的传统职业培训正在逐渐衰落，导致成千上万未上大学而寻求手艺培训的年轻人陷入困境。就大学而言，自 1985 年以来毕业的化学、机械、工业和冶金（冶金）工程师越来越少，部分原因是他们的大雇主制造业的作用下降。这种衰退始于 20 世纪 50 年代，当时制造业创造了国民收入或国内生产总值的 28%，雇用了三分之一的劳动力。如今，工厂产出仅占 GDP 的 12%，雇用的工人仅占全国的 9%。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Mass layoffs and plant closings have drawn plenty of headlines and public debate over the years, and they still occasionally do. But the damage to skill and craftsmanship — what’s needed to build a complex airliner or a tractor, or for a worker to move up from assembler to machinist to supervisor — went largely unnoticed.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 多年来，大规模裁员和工厂关闭已经引起了大量的头条新闻和公众辩论，而且现在仍然偶尔如此。但对技能和工艺的损害——建造复杂的客机或拖拉机，或者工人从装配工晋升到机械师再到主管所需的技能和工艺——基本上没有被注意到。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) “In an earlier generation, we lost our connection to the land, and now we are losing our connection to the machinery we depend on,” says Michael Hout, a sociologist at the University of California, Berkeley. “People who work with their hands,” he went on, “are doing things today that we call service jobs, in restaurants and laundries, or in medical technology and the like.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H）“在上一代人中，我们失去了与土地的联系，现在我们正在失去与我们所依赖的机器的联系，”加州大学伯克利分校的社会学家迈克尔·豪特说。他继续说道：“今天，用手工作的人正在做我们称之为服务工作的事情，比如在餐馆、洗衣店或医疗技术等领域。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) That’s one explanation for the decline in traditional craftsmanship. Lack of interest is another. The big money is in fields like finance. Starting in the 1980s, skill in finance grew in importance, and, as depicted in the news media and the movies, became a more appealing source of income. By last year, Wall Street traders, bankers and those who deal in real estate generated 21% of the national income, double their share in the 1950s. And Warren Buffett, the good-natured financier, became a homespun folk hero, without the tools and overalls (工作服).
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 这是传统手工艺衰落的一种解释。缺乏兴趣是另一回事。大笔资金集中在金融等领域。从 20 世纪 80 年代开始，金融技能变得越来越重要，并且正如新闻媒体和电影中所描述的那样，成为更有吸引力的收入来源。到去年，华尔街交易员、银行家和房地产交易者创造了 21% 的国民收入，是 20 世纪 50 年代所占份额的两倍。沃伦·巴菲特，这位心地善良的金融家，在没有工具和工作服的情况下，成为了一位朴素的民间英雄。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) “Young people grow up without developing the skills to fix things around the house,” says Richard Curtin, director of the Thomson Reuters/University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers. “They know about computers, of course, but they don’t know how to build them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 汤森路透/密歇根大学消费者调查中心主任理查德·科廷 (Richard Curtin) 表示：“年轻人在成长过程中并没有培养出修理家务的技能。” “当然，他们了解计算机，但他们不知道如何构建它们。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Manufacturing’s shrinking presence undoubtedly helps explain the decline in craftsmanship, if only because many of the nation’s assembly line workers were skilled in craft work, if not on the job then in their spare time. In a late 1990s
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 制造业的萎缩无疑有助于解释手工艺的衰落，因为这个国家的许多装配线工人都精通手工艺，即使不是在工作中，也是在业余时间。在 20 世纪 90 年代末

paragraphs.sourceText: study of blue-collar employees at a General Motors plant (now closed) in Linden, NJ, the sociologist Ruth Milkman of City University of New York found that many line workers, in their off-hours, did home renovation and other skilled work. “I have often thought,” Ms Milkman says, “that these extracurricular jobs were an effort on the part of the workers to regain their dignity after suffering the degradation of repetitive assembly line work in the factory.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 纽约城市大学的社会学家露丝·米尔克曼（Ruth Milkman）对新泽西州林登通用汽车工厂（现已关闭）的蓝领员工进行的研究发现，许多生产线工人在下班时间从事房屋装修和其他技术性工作。 “我经常想，”米尔克曼女士说，“这些课外工作是工人们在经历了工厂重复性流水线工作的退化之后，为了重获尊严而做出的努力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Craft work has higher status in nations like Germany, which invests in apprenticeship（学徒）programmes for high school students. “Corporations in Germany realised that there was an interest to be served economically and patriotically in building up a skilled labour force at home; we never had that ethos（风气）,”says Richard Sennett, a New York University sociologist who has written about the connection of craft and culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 手工艺工作在德国等国家享有更高的地位，这些国家投资于高中生的学徒计划。 “德国的企业意识到，在国内建立一支熟练的劳动力队伍可以在经济和爱国方面得到满足；但我们从来没有这种风气，”纽约大学社会学家理查德·森内特（Richard Sennett）说，他曾撰写过有关手工艺与文化联系的文章。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) The damage to American craftsmanship seems to parallel the steep slide in manufacturing employment. Though the decline started in the 1970s, it became much steeper beginning in 2000. Since then, some 5.3 million jobs, or one-third of the workforce in manufacturing, have been lost. A stated goal of the Obama administration is to restore a big chunk of this employment, along with the multitude of skills that many of the jobs required.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）对美国手工艺的损害似乎与制造业就业的急剧下滑同时发生。尽管下降始于 2000 年代，但从 2000 年开始下降幅度更大。自那时起，大约有 530 万个工作岗位（即制造业劳动力的三分之一）消失了。奥巴马政府的既定目标是恢复大部分就业，以及许多工作所需的多种技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) As for craftsmanship itself, the issue is how to preserve it as a valued skill in the general population. Ms Milkman, the sociologist, argues that American craftsmanship isn’t disappearing as quickly as some would argue — that it has instead shifted to immigrants. “Pride in craft, it is alive in the immigrant world,” she says.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 至于手工艺本身，问题是如何将其保留为普通大众的宝贵技能。社会学家米尔克曼女士认为，美国的手工艺并没有像某些人认为的那样消失得那么快，而是已经转移到了移民手中。 “对工艺的自豪感在移民世界中依然存在，”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Sol Axelrod, 37, the manager of the Home Depot here, fittingly learned to fix his own car as a teenager, even changing the brakes. Now he finds immigrant craftsmen. gathered in abundance outside his store in the early morning, waiting for it to open so they can buy supplies for the day’s work as contractors. Skilled day laborers, also mostly immigrants, wait quietly in hopes of being hired by the contractors. Mr Axelrod also says the recession and persistently high unemployment have forced many people to try to save money by doing more themselves, and Home Depot in response offers classes in fixing water taps and other simple repairs. The teachers are store employees, many of them older and semi-retired from a skilled trade, or laid off. “Our customers may not be building cabinets or outdoor decks; we try to do that for them,’’ Mr Axelrod says, “but some are trying to build up skill so they can do more for themselves in these hard times.”
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 索尔·阿克塞尔罗德 (Sol Axelrod)，37 岁，是这里家得宝 (Home Depot) 的经理，十几岁时就学会了修理自己的汽车，甚至更换刹车。现在他找到了移民工匠。清晨，大量人聚集在他的商店外面，等待商店开门，这样他们就可以购买承包商当天工作所需的物资。熟练的临时工（大多是移民）静静地等待，希望被承包商雇用。阿克塞尔罗德还表示，经济衰退和持续居高不下的失业率迫使许多人试图通过自己做更多的事情来省钱，为此，家得宝提供了修理水龙头和其他简单维修的课程。这些老师都是商店员工，其中许多人年龄较大，从熟练行业半退休，或者下岗。阿克塞尔罗德先生说：“我们的客户可能不会建造橱柜或户外露台；我们会尽力为他们做这件事，但有些人正在努力培养技能，以便在困难时期为自己做更多事情。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Mastering tools and working with one’s hands shapes people’s thinking and behaviour.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46、掌握工具、亲力亲为塑造人的思维和行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. The factor that people can earn more money in fields other than manufacturing contributes to the decline in traditional craftsmanship.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 人们可以在制造业以外的领域赚更多钱，这一因素导致了传统手工艺的衰落。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. According to the author, manufacturing encourages craftsmanship.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 作者认为，制造业鼓励手工艺。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. According to Ruth Milkman, American craftsmanship, instead of disappearing, is being taken up by immigrants.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 据露丝·米尔克曼 (Ruth Milkman) 称，美国的手工艺不但没有消失，反而被移民所继承。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. The White House welcomed Ford’s announcement to bring some production back to America.

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. According to Mr Axelrod of Home Depot, people are trying to ride out the recession by doing more themselves.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The report from the Bureau of Labour Statistics was just as gloomy as anticipated. Unemployment in January jumped to a 16-year high of 7.6 percent, as 598,000 jobs were slashed from U.S. payrolls in the worst single-month decline since December, 1974. With 1.8 million jobs lost in the last three months, there is urgent desire to boost the economy as quickly as possible. But Washington would do well to take a deep breath before reacting to the grim numbers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国劳工统计局的报告正如预期的一样悲观。 1月份失业率跃升至7.6%，创16年新高，美国就业人数减少59.8万，创1974年12月以来最严重单月降幅。过去三个月失业人数达180万，人们迫切希望尽快提振经济。但在对严峻的数字做出反应之前，华盛顿最好先深吸一口气。

paragraphs.sourceText: Collectively, we rely on the unemployment figures and other statistics to frame our sense of reality. They are a vital part of an array of data that we use to assess if we’re doing well or doing badly, and that in turn shapes government policies and corporate budgets and personal spending decisions. The problem is that the statistics aren’t an objective measure of reality; they are simply a best approximation. Directionally, they capture the trends, but the idea that we know precisely how many are unemployed is a myth. That makes finding a solution all the more difficult.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总的来说，我们依靠失业数据和其他统计数据来构建我们的现实感。它们是一系列数据的重要组成部分，我们用这些数据来评估我们做得好还是不好，进而影响政府政策、企业预算和个人支出决策。问题在于统计数据并不能客观地衡量现实情况。它们只是一个最佳近似值。从方向上来说，他们捕捉了趋势，但我们确切知道有多少人失业的想法是一个神话。这使得寻找解决方案变得更加困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: First, there is the way the data is assembled. The official unemployment rate is the product of a telephone survey of about 60,000 homes. There is another survey, sometimes referred to as the “payroll survey”, that assesses 400,000 businesses based on their reported payrolls. Both surveys have problems. The payroll survey can easily double-count someone: if you are one person with two jobs, you show up as two workers. The payroll survey also doesn’t capture the number of self- employed, and so says little about how many people are generating an independent income.
paragraphs.translationZh: 首先，是数据的组装方式。官方失业率是对约 60,000 个家庭进行电话调查的结果。还有另一项调查，有时称为“工资调查”，根据 400,000 家企业报告的工资单对其进行评估。两项调查都存在问题。工资调查很容易重复计算某人：如果你是一个人从事两份工作，那么你就会显示为两名工人。工资调查也没有统计个体经营者的数量，因此很少说明有多少人正在产生独立收入。

paragraphs.sourceText: The household survey has a larger problem. When asked straightforwardly, people tend to lie or shade the truth when the subject is sex, money or employment. If you get a call and are asked if you’re employed, and you say yes, you’re employed. If you say no, however, it may surprise you to learn that you are only unemployed if you’ve been actively looking for work in the past four weeks; otherwise, you are “marginally attached to the labour force” and not actually unemployed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 家庭调查有一个更大的问题。当被直接询问时，当话题涉及性、金钱或就业时，人们往往会撒谎或掩盖真相。如果您接到电话并询问您是否受雇，并且您说是，那么您就受雇了。然而，如果您拒绝，您可能会惊讶地发现，只有在过去四个星期内一直在积极寻找工作的情况下，您才会失业；否则，你只是“边缘依附于劳动力”，而不是真正失业。

paragraphs.sourceText: The urge to quantify is embedded in our society. But the idea that statisticians can then capture an objective reality isn’t just impossible. It also leads to serious misjudgments. Democrats and Republicans can and will take sides on a number of issues, but a more crucial concern is that both are basing major policy decisions on guesstimates rather than looking at the vast wealth of raw data with a critical eye and an open mind.
paragraphs.translationZh: 量化的冲动根植于我们的社会。但统计学家能够捕捉客观现实的想法并非不可能。这也会导致严重的误判。民主党和共和党可以而且将会在许多问题上选边站，但更重要的担忧是，双方都将重大政策决策建立在猜测的基础上，而不是以批判的眼光和开放的心态来看待大量的原始数据。

Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: At some point in 2008, someone, probably in either Asia or Africa, made the decision to move from the countryside to the city. This nameless person pushed the human race over a historic threshold, for it was in that year that mankind became, for the first time in its history, a predominantly urban species.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2008 年的某个时候，有人（可能来自亚洲或非洲）决定从农村搬到城市。这个无名的人将人类推向了一个历史性的门槛，因为正是在那一年，人类在其历史上第一次成为一个以城市为主的物种。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is a trend that shows no sign of slowing. Demographers(人口统计学家）reckon that three-quarters of humanity could be city-dwelling by 2050, with most of the increase coming in the fast-growing towns of Asia and Africa. Migrants to cities are attracted by plentiful jobs, access to hospitals and education, and the ability to escape the boredom of a farmer’s agricultural life. Those factors are more than enough to make up for the squalor（肮脏）disease and spectacular poverty that those same migrants must often at first endure when they become urban dwellers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一趋势没有放缓的迹象。人口统计学家估计，到 2050 年，四分之三的人口可能居住在城市，其中大部分增长来自亚洲和非洲快速发展的城镇。大量的工作、就医和教育的机会以及摆脱农民农业生活的无聊的能力吸引了移民到城市。这些因素足以弥补这些移民所面临的肮脏疾病和巨大贫困。当他们成为城市居民时，往往首先必须忍受。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is the city that inspires the latest book from Peter Smith. His main thesis is that the buzz of urban life, and the opportunities it offers for cooperation and collaboration, is what attracts people to the city, which in turn makes cities into the engines of art, commerce, science and progress. This is hardly revolutionary, but it is presented in a charming format. Mr Smith has written a breezy guidebook, with a series of short chapters dedicated to specific aspects of urbanity — parks, say, or the various schemes that have been put forward over the years for building the perfect city. The result is a sort of high-quality, unusually rigorous coffee-table book, designed to be dipped into rather than read from beginning to end.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正是这座城市为彼得·史密斯的最新著作提供了灵感。他的主要论点是，城市生活的喧嚣及其提供的合作机会是吸引人们来到城市的原因，这反过来又使城市成为艺术、商业、科学和进步的引擎。这算不上革命性的，但它以一种迷人的形式呈现。史密斯先生写了一本轻松活泼的指南，其中有一系列简短的章节专门讨论城市化的具体方面——比如公园，或者多年来为建设完美城市而提出的各种计划。结果是一本高质量、异常严格的咖啡桌书，其设计目的是为了深入阅读，而不是从头到尾阅读。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the chapter on skyscrapers, for example, Mr Smith touches on construction methods, the revolutionary invention of the automatic lift, the practicalities of living in the sky and the likelihood that, as cities become more crowded, apartment living will become the norm. But there is also time for brief diversions onto bizarre ground, such as a discussion of the skyscraper index (which holds that a boom in skyscraper construction is a foolproof sign of an imminent recession).
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，在关于摩天大楼的章节中，史密斯先生谈到了建筑方法、自动电梯的革命性发明、空中生活的实用性，以及随着城市变得更加拥挤，公寓生活将成为常态的可能性。但也有时间短暂地转移到一些奇怪的话题上，比如讨论摩天大楼指数（该指数认为摩天大楼建设的繁荣是经济衰退即将来临的万无一失的迹象）。

paragraphs.sourceText: One obvious criticism is that the price of breadth is depth: many of Mr Smith’s essays raise as many questions as they answer. Although that can indeed be frustrating, this is probably the only way to treat so grand a topic. The city is the building block of civilisation and of almost everything people do; a guidebook to the city is really, therefore, a guidebook to how a large and ever-growing chunk of humanity chooses to live. Mr Smiths book serves as an excellent introduction to a vast subject, and will suggest plenty of further lines of inquiry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个明显的批评是，广度的代价就是深度：史密斯先生的许多文章提出的问题和他们回答的问题一样多。尽管这确实令人沮丧，但这可能是处理如此宏大的话题的唯一方法。城市是文明的基石，也是人们所做的几乎所有事情的基石。因此，一本城市指南实际上是一本关于越来越多的人类选择如何生活的指南。史密斯先生的书是对一个广阔主题的精彩介绍，并将提出大量进一步的探究线索。
